name: יוֹרָה
summary: The head of a family of 112 who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezr 2:18). In the same list in Nehemiah the family is “the sons of חָרִיף”, again 112 (Neh 7:24): חָרִיף is the word of חֹרֶף, the autumn and winter season of ploughing (Gen 8:22; Pro 20:4), and יוֹרָה is the spelling of יוֹרֶה, the early rain that falls in that season (Deu 11:14). The two names of one family both seem to name the autumn; scripture does not explain either.

evidence.note: “The sons of יוֹרָה, a hundred and twelve.”
The same place in the list: “The sons of חָרִיף, a hundred and twelve.”
“I will give the rain of your land in its season, יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ.”
“Seed and harvest, cold and heat, summer and חֹרֶף.”

note: TIPNR's Jorah@Ezr.2.18 record carries both forms, Jorah and Hariph (Neh 7:24). The Hariph of Neh 10:20 is a separate TIPNR person (Hariph@Neh.10.19) and is not tagged. The reading “early rain” takes יוֹרָה as a by-form of יוֹרֶה, supported by the Hariph parallel (חָרִיף, root חרף “autumn”); it is a reading of the form, not stated in scripture.
